irrišūtum: tenancy, cultivation on lease: ana irrišūtim “for cultivation (as a tenant)”
waṣûm-Š: Š-stem of waṣûm “to go out”: to send out, bring out; of land, to take on lease: ana irrišūtim ušēṣi “he took (a field) for cultivation”
itûm: neighbour, the adjoining one: kīma itêšu “like its neighbour” (the neighbouring field)
mayyārum: a tilling implement — uncertain: Harper “hoe”, later dictionaries a breaking-plough; mayyārī “with ploughs”
maḫāṣum: to strike; of ground, to break up: imaḫḫaṣ “he shall break up”
nidûtum: uncultivated, fallow land — Harper’s reading of KI.KAL (which he also gives as KANKAL); later dictionaries read the logogram as kankallum “hard, uncultivated land”
teptītum: opening-up, bringing waste land into cultivation: teptītim “for opening-up”
aḫum: arm, side: aḫšu iddi “he let his arm drop” = he was idle, negligent
petûm: to open; of land, to bring into cultivation: iptete “he has opened”
rebûm: fourth: rebûtim šattim “in the fourth year”
marārum: to hoe, break clods: imarrar “he shall hoe”
10: ten — one corner-wedge (U); said ešret (?) with a masculine noun, ešer with a feminine one (Akkadian 3–10 take the opposite gender’s form): 10 ŠE.GUR “ten kor of grain”. Before a field-measure the wedge may count bur-units rather than tens (see §44)
būrum: the bur, a field measure (written GAN.E; Harper reads GAN, 1,800 SAR, about 6⅔ acres): būrim
kurrum: the kor, a grain measure (written GUR; Harper: 300 KA): kur šeʾam “a kor of grain”
madādum: to measure out (grain): imaddad “he shall measure out”
irrišum: tenant, cultivator: irrišum, ana irrišim “to a tenant”; irrissu “his tenant” (irriš + -šu; Harper reads the same spelling as a verb, “he shall cultivate it”)
raḫāṣum: to flood, wash over: irtaḫiṣ “(Adad) has flooded”
bibbulum: flood, high water — uncertain: later dictionaries “flood”, Harper “produce”; bibbulum
apšitûm: proportion, agreed share — uncertain and rare: Harper “agreement (?)”; apšitêm, ana apšitêm “in the (agreed) proportion”
zâzum: to divide, share: izuzzū “they shall divide”
maḫrûm: first, former, previous: maḫrītim in šattim maḫrītim “in the previous year”
mānaḫtum: toil, outlay, upkeep: mānaḫātišu “his upkeep (outlay)”; mānaḫat erēšim “the cost of cultivating”
apāsum-D: D-stem (Harper’s apāsum II,1), a rare verb of uncertain meaning: ul uppas “he shall not object/interfere” — sense from context; Harper “interfere”
erēšum-N: N-stem of erēšum “to cultivate”: to be cultivated: inneriš “it was cultivated”
ebūrum: harvest, the crop: ebūrim “of harvest, at harvest” (one logogram, read BURU₁₄; Harper writes ebûrim)
ḫubullum: debt, an interest-bearing loan: ḫubullum; bēl ḫubullim “the creditor”
raṭābum-D: D-stem of raṭābum “to be wet”: to moisten (a clay tablet, so it can be rewritten): uraṭṭab “he shall wet”; Harper reads u-ra-ad-da-ab
epšētum: works, tilling: eqel epšētim “a field of works”, a field already prepared
šamaššammū: sesame, the oil-plant: šamaššammam, šamaššammim (written ŠE.GIŠ.Ì; Harper ŠE.IZ.NI)
eršum: cultivated, sown: eqlam eršam “a sown field”
maḫīrum: market rate, price: ana maḫīrātišunu “at their rates”
ṣimdatum: royal ordinance, regulation: ṣimdat šarrim “the king’s ordinance” (Harper: “scale”)

__broaden__.3-kam: the 3rd; MU III{kam} “the third year” (KAM marks ordinals, as in §13) · also a plain count: ana MU 3{kam} “for three years”, said šalāš šanātim (spoken form reconstructed)
__broaden__.nadûm: to cast, throw (a charge; a body into the river): iddi, nadû, iddû · also to leave lying (a field): ittadi “he has left (it) lying”
__broaden__.tabālum: to take away, carry off: itabbal · tabal “take!” (imperative)
__broaden__.bēlum: owner, lord: bēl ḫulqim “owner of the lost property” · owner of a field, bēl eqlim; bēl ḫubullim “creditor”
__broaden__.šaluštum: one-third: šalušti eqlim “a third of the field” — the widow’s child-raising portion · also a third of the crop in a sharecrop lease: šaluš
__broaden__.pûm: mouth (the KA sign); ina pī mātim “in the mouth of the land” · ana pî ṣimdat šarrim “according to the mouth of the king’s ordinance”

bašûm-Š: Š-stem of bašûm “to exist”: to bring into being, produce (a crop): uštabši “he has produced” (perfect)
